title: CloudTrail/Activity Log Event Volume Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.6.6 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.6.6 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS, Azure Activity Log add-on; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for AWS, Azure Activity Log add-on
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" readOnly=false
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.6_cloudtrail_activity_log_6"
| sort -_time
description: Management event volume over 90 days highlights automation changes, new integrations, or possible abuse such as enumeration or bulk API use. Baselines help spot anomalies without reading every event.
value: Detecting cloudtrail/activity log event volume trending early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Filter to non-read-only events for management actions. For multi-cloud, use union or a combined index with sourcetype in the by clause. Chart 90 days with daily span. Alert on statistical outliers exceeding 3x baseline. Ensure CloudTrail is multi-region and organization trails where applicable so the trend is complete. For Azure, include Activity Log management category events.
visualization: Line chart (daily management events with 7-day SMA, 90 days), anomaly overlay, 14-day forecast.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS, Azure Activity Log add-on with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.6.7.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Filter to non-read-only events for management actions. For multi-cloud, use union or a combined index with sourcetype in the by clause. Chart 90 days with daily span. Alert on statistical outliers exceeding 3x baseline. Ensure CloudTrail is multi-region and organization trails where applicable so the trend is complete. For Azure, include Activity Log management category events.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" readOnly=false
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.6_cloudtrail_activity_log_6"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=cloud` to detect cloudtrail/activity log event volume trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_6_6_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (daily management events with 7-day SMA, 90 days), anomaly overlay, 14-day forecast..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS, Azure Activity Log add-on and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloudtrail/activity log event volume trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
